intent: Turn the Python tests CI workflow green. It has failed since ~2026-08-19 in 'Install dependencies' with pip's resolution-too-deep error, so no Python test has actually run in CI for days.
scope: meta/requirements.txt (root requirements.txt is a symlink to it)
Non-goal: pinning the other 78 unpinned dependencies, which would be a much larger change
changes: Removed mitmproxy>=10.0. The CI log shows the resolver backtracking endlessly through Brotli 1.0.6/1.0.4/1.0.1 and asgiref 3.8.0/3.7.1/3.6.0, all pulled in by mitmproxy, before giving up.
It is safe to remove: nothing under python_pkg/ imports mitmproxy, and `git grep mitmproxy` finds it only in a pacman whitelist and a docs file. check_requirements_sync.py passes without it.

verification.command: python3.11 -m venv; pip install --dry-run -r <requirements WITH mitmproxy>
verification.evidence: exit 1, 'error: resolution-too-deep' -- the CI failure reproduced locally on Python 3.11.11 with pip 26.2.1, the same versions CI uses

verification.command: pip install --dry-run -r <requirements WITHOUT mitmproxy> in the same venv

verification.evidence: exit 0 -- no python_pkg import needs the dropped package

risks: If a future script wants mitmproxy it must be re-added, and the resolver problem returns. Pinning it to an exact version would be the way back in.
The underlying fragility remains: 78 of 80 requirements are unpinned >= ranges, so another wide-dependency package could reintroduce this.
rollback: Re-add 'mitmproxy>=10.0' to meta/requirements.txt in sorted position.
Expect Python tests CI to go red again at the Install dependencies step.
